# Loadout — full content

## AI Code Editors & IDEs
- **Cursor** (freemium) — AI code editor and coding agent platform; hand off tasks to agents or code alongside them. Best for: Day-to-day coding with an agent inside your editor. https://cursor.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)** (freemium) — Cognition's IDE (Windsurf renamed June 2026) with an Agent Command Center for managing local and cloud agents. Best for: Managing multiple agents from a full IDE. https://devin.ai/desktop (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **GitHub Copilot** (freemium) — AI pair programmer in VS Code, JetBrains and GitHub, with chat and agent mode. Best for: Teams already living on GitHub. https://github.com/features/copilot (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Zed** (freemium) — Fast, Rust-built collaborative code editor with built-in AI assistance. Best for: Speed-focused devs who want AI without bloat. https://zed.dev (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **JetBrains Air** (freemium) — JetBrains' agentic development environment for running Claude Agent, Codex, Junie, Copilot and ACP agents, in IDEs, browser or CLI. Best for: JetBrains users orchestrating coding agents. https://www.jetbrains.com/air/ (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Kiro** (freemium) — AWS's agentic IDE built around spec-driven development. Best for: Turning a spec into structured code. https://kiro.dev (verified: 2026-10-15)

## App Builders (Prompt-to-App)
- **Lovable** (freemium) — Build full-stack web apps by chatting, with Supabase integration. Best for: Non-coders shipping a real web app. https://lovable.dev (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Bolt.new** (freemium) — StackBlitz's in-browser prompt-to-app builder that runs code in WebContainers. Best for: Fast prototypes in the browser. https://bolt.new (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **v0** (freemium) — Vercel's generative UI and app builder producing React/Next.js code. Best for: Next.js UIs you can deploy to Vercel. https://v0.app (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Replit** (freemium) — Cloud IDE with Replit Agent that builds and deploys apps from prompts. Best for: Build-and-host in one place. https://replit.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Base44** (freemium) — No-code AI app builder that generates apps with built-in backend. Best for: Internal tools and simple apps, no setup. https://base44.com (verified: 2026-10-15)

## Coding Agents
- **Claude Code** (paid) — Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal and IDEs. Best for: Large, multi-step coding tasks from the terminal. https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **OpenAI Codex** (paid) — OpenAI's coding agent across ChatGPT, CLI, IDE extension and cloud; included in ChatGPT plans. Best for: Delegating tasks and automated PR review. https://openai.com/codex/ (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **OpenCode** (free) — Open-source, model-agnostic coding agent with terminal, desktop and web apps. Best for: Open-source agent with any model. https://opencode.ai (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Cline** (free) — Open-source autonomous coding agent for VS Code; bring your own model. Best for: Transparent agent inside VS Code. https://cline.bot (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Aider** (free) — Open-source AI pair programming in your terminal with git integration. Best for: Git-native terminal pair programming. https://aider.chat (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Devin** (freemium) — Cognition's autonomous coding agent running parallel cloud agents. Best for: Hands-off async engineering tasks. https://devin.ai (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Jules** (freemium) — Google's asynchronous coding agent that works on your GitHub repos. Best for: Background fixes on GitHub repos. https://jules.google (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Amp** (freemium) — Sourcegraph's agentic coding tool for terminal and editors. Best for: Frontier-model agent work. https://ampcode.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **heal.dev** (free) — Bug-hunting agent that learns to run your app in a production-like sandbox, then finds bugs, runtime vulnerabilities and performance issues, each filed with a failing test that proves it. Free during the beta. Best for: Catching runtime bugs that code review misses. https://heal.dev (verified: 2026-10-23)
- **Corgi** (free) — Terminal multiplexer for running coding agents: tabs for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi with live status (working, needs you, finished), token usage, file-change replay and worktrees, and sessions keep running in the background like tmux. macOS, Linux and WSL. Best for: Watching several coding agents at once. https://corgi.computer (verified: 2026-10-24)
- **Reason** (freemium) — Cost-efficient coding agent that writes code, runs tests and opens PRs from Mac, terminal, web or Slack. Best for: Cost-efficient autonomous coding and PRs. https://reasonmachines.com (verified: 2026-10-15)

## Agent Frameworks
- **LangGraph** (free) — Framework from LangChain for building stateful, multi-step agent graphs. Best for: Controllable production agents. https://www.langchain.com/langgraph (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **CrewAI** (freemium) — Open-source multi-agent framework plus a paid hosted platform. Best for: Multi-agent teams quickly. https://www.crewai.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **OpenAI Agents SDK** (free) — Lightweight SDK for building agents with tools, handoffs and guardrails. Best for: Agents on OpenAI models. https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/ (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Mastra** (free) — TypeScript framework for AI agents, workflows and RAG. Best for: JS/TS developers building agents. https://mastra.ai (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Vercel AI SDK** (free) — TypeScript toolkit for building AI apps and agents across model providers. Best for: AI features in Next.js/React apps. https://ai-sdk.dev (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Agent-Native** (free) — Builder.io's open-source TypeScript framework for agentic apps where agent and UI share actions, data and state. Best for: Building agentic apps with a real UI. https://www.agent-native.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **NitroStack** (freemium) — Full-stack platform for MCP servers: open-source TypeScript and Python SDK and CLI, NitroStudio for visual testing, and NitroCloud hosting with GitHub deploys and scale-to-zero. Best for: Building, testing and hosting your own MCP server. https://nitrostack.ai (verified: 2026-10-18)
- **Omnara** (freemium) — Open-source managed agent platform: one API to run agents on any model and any machine, with tools, secrets, permissions and streaming built in. Self-hostable alternative to Claude Managed Agents. Best for: Running agents for your users without building the infra. https://www.omnara.com (verified: 2026-10-22)

## Deploy, Hosting & Backend
- **Vercel** (freemium) — Frontend cloud for deploying Next.js and other web apps. Best for: Deploying frontends in one click. https://vercel.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Netlify** (freemium) — Platform for deploying and hosting web apps and sites. Best for: Static and Jamstack sites. https://www.netlify.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Supabase** (freemium) — Open-source Postgres backend with auth, storage and edge functions. Best for: Backend for vibe-coded apps. https://supabase.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Convex** (freemium) — Reactive backend platform with database and server functions in TypeScript; open source. Best for: Realtime apps in TypeScript. https://www.convex.dev (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Cloudflare Workers** (freemium) — Serverless platform for running code at the edge, including agents. Best for: Cheap global serverless + agents. https://workers.cloudflare.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Railway** (freemium) — Deploy apps, databases and services from a repo with minimal config. Best for: Hosting backends without DevOps. https://railway.com (verified: 2026-10-15)

## Design-to-Code
- **Figma Make** (freemium) — Figma's prompt-to-app tool that turns designs and prompts into working prototypes. Best for: Designers turning ideas into prototypes. https://www.figma.com/make/ (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Builder.io** (freemium) — Visual development platform that converts Figma designs to code. Best for: Figma-to-production code. https://www.builder.io (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Locofy** (freemium) — Converts Figma/Penpot designs into frontend code. Best for: Design handoff to React/HTML. https://www.locofy.ai (verified: no)

## AI APIs & Models
- **Anthropic API (Claude)** (paid) — API access to Claude models, strong at coding and agentic work. Best for: Powering coding agents. https://www.anthropic.com/api (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **OpenAI API** (paid) — API for GPT models, embeddings, images and realtime voice. Best for: General-purpose AI features. https://platform.openai.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Google Gemini API** (freemium) — Gemini models via Google AI Studio with long context and a free tier. Best for: Long context and generous free tier. https://ai.google.dev (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **OpenRouter** (freemium) — Single API to access hundreds of models from many providers. Best for: Swapping models behind one key. https://openrouter.ai (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **DeepSeek API** (paid) — Low-cost DeepSeek V4 models (1M context) with OpenAI- and Anthropic-format endpoints, so it plugs into Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode; also sells per-request Search and Fetch APIs. Best for: Cheap model calls for coding agents. https://api-docs.deepseek.com (verified: 2026-10-18)
- **Groq** (freemium) — Fast inference cloud for open models, built on its LPU hardware. Best for: Low-latency responses. https://groq.com (verified: no)
- **Opper** (freemium) — Access 700+ leading AI models through one EU-hosted API, pay-as-you-go. GDPR-compliant, with spend caps, model allowlists and zero data retention. Best for: EU-hosted access to many models behind one API. https://opper.ai (verified: 2026-10-21)

## Sports AI Tools
- **BALLDONTLIE** (freemium) — Sports data API for 20+ leagues (NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL, soccer, esports and more) with odds, an OpenAPI spec built for AI assistants, and a free tier. Best for: Stats and odds data for sports shows and apps. https://www.balldontlie.io (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **API-Sports** (freemium) — REST sports data APIs covering 2,000+ competitions with live scores, odds and free widgets; free plan of 100 requests/day per API, paid from $10/month. Best for: Cheap live scores and stats across many sports. https://api-sports.io (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **StoryStats** (freemium) — Automated sports writer that turns game data into ready-to-publish stories for NBA, WNBA, MLB, NHL, NFL and soccer; free start, $30/month per sport. Best for: Auto-written game previews and recaps. https://www.storystats.ai (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Castmagic** (paid) — AI that turns podcast audio and video into show notes, clips, posts and other content. Best for: Repurposing each episode into posts and show notes. https://www.castmagic.io (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **OpusClip** (freemium) — AI video clipping tool that turns long videos into short clips with captions, reframing and a social scheduler. Best for: Turning episodes into shorts. https://www.opus.pro (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Descript** (freemium) — Text-based video and audio editor with multitrack podcast editing, remote recording, transcription and captions. Best for: Editing and recording podcast episodes. https://www.descript.com (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **Magnifi** (paid) — AI video tagging and automated sports highlights platform, now part of Sportz Interactive; demo-based sales. Best for: Media teams automating highlight production. https://magnifi.ai (verified: 2026-10-15)
- **WSC Sports** (paid) — AI platform for creating, managing and distributing sports highlights, used by 650 teams, leagues and broadcasters; demo-based sales. Best for: Leagues and broadcasters scaling highlights. https://www.wsc-sports.com (verified: 2026-10-15)

## Agent Tools
- **Postiz** (paid) — Social media scheduler with a hosted MCP server, CLI, public API and webhooks on every plan, so agents can schedule posts across X, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Bluesky and more. Best for: Letting an agent post to social channels for you. https://postiz.com (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Ayrshare** (paid) — Social media API for products and AI platforms: post, schedule, pull analytics and moderate comments across 14+ networks, billed per social profile. Best for: Apps that post to social on behalf of their users. https://www.ayrshare.com (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **AgentValley** (free) — Free, open-source Mac app that lives in your MacBook's notch and shows every Claude Code session and sub-agent at a glance: which model it's on, its latest step, and a red count when one is waiting on you. macOS 15+, Claude Code only. Best for: Keeping tabs on several Claude Code sessions at once. https://agentvalley.app (verified: 2026-10-25)
- **Resend** (freemium) — Email API for developers with transactional and marketing email, plus inboxes your agents can send, receive and reply from via API and MCP. Best for: Giving an app or agent a reliable email API. https://resend.com (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **AgentMail** (freemium) — Email inboxes built for AI agents, with an API, SDKs, an MCP server, threads, drafts, webhooks and custom domains. Best for: Giving each agent its own inbox. https://www.agentmail.to (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Stripe** (paid) — Payments platform with an MCP server, agent plugin and agent skills, plus tools to sell through agents and accept agent-initiated payments. Best for: Letting agents work with payments, billing and checkout. https://stripe.com (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Twilio** (paid) — Communications APIs for voice calls, SMS, WhatsApp and verification, plus Conversation Relay for plugging voice AI into calls. Best for: Phone numbers, calls and texts for an agent. https://www.twilio.com (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Vapi** (freemium) — Developer platform for building voice AI agents that make and take phone calls; pick your own transcriber, model and voice providers. Best for: Building custom voice agents on the phone. https://vapi.ai (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Bland AI** (freemium) — AI phone call platform with one per-minute rate that covers the model, transcription and voice; bring your own Twilio or SIP or use Bland's. Best for: Phone agents with simple all-in pricing. https://www.bland.ai (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Browserbase** (freemium) — Cloud headless browsers for agents, plus Search and Fetch APIs; makers of the open-source Stagehand browser-agent SDK. Best for: Running fleets of browsers for web agents. https://www.browserbase.com (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Browser Use** (paid) — Cloud browsers and browser agents that complete web tasks, billed pay-as-you-go with no subscription. Best for: Cheap pay-as-you-go browser agents. https://browser-use.com (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Firecrawl** (freemium) — Web data API that searches, scrapes, crawls and maps sites into LLM-ready content for agents. Best for: Turning web pages into clean data for an agent. https://www.firecrawl.dev (verified: 2026-10-17)
- **Pomerado** (freemium) — Turns websites with no API, from consumer sites to legacy portals, into tested API and MCP tools your agents can call, with sign-in (including 2FA) handled. Open source. Best for: Letting an agent use websites that have no API. https://pomerado.ai (verified: 2026-10-17)

## Which tool should I use
- I can't code but want to ship a web app: Lovable > Bolt.new > Replit
- I code daily and want an AI editor: Cursor > Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) > GitHub Copilot
- I want an agent to handle big tasks in my repo: Claude Code > OpenAI Codex > OpenCode
- I want a free/open-source coding agent: OpenCode > Cline > Aider
- I need a backend + database fast: Supabase > Convex > Railway
- I want to deploy my app: Vercel > Netlify > Cloudflare Workers
- I'm building my own AI agent: Agent-Native > Vercel AI SDK > Mastra
- I want to turn a design into code: Figma Make > Builder.io > Locofy
- Which model API should power my app?: Anthropic API (Claude) > OpenAI API > Google Gemini API
- I run a sports podcast or channel: Descript > OpusClip > Castmagic > BALLDONTLIE

## Guides
- [Best AI coding tool for your first SaaS](https://loadoutweekly.com/best-ai-coding-tool-first-saas/): Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Lovable, Bolt, Replit and v0 compared for first-time builders, with official prices checked Oct 17, 2026.

## Comparisons
- **Cursor vs Devin Desktop (2026)** — Cursor (freemium) — AI code editor and coding agent platform; hand off tasks to agents or code alongside them. Best for: Day-to-day coding with an agent inside your editor. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) (freemium) — Cognition's IDE (Windsurf renamed June 2026) with an Agent Command Center for managing local and cloud agents. Best for: Managing multiple agents from a full IDE. Editorial comparison; rankings and picks are never sold. https://loadoutweekly.com/compare/cursor-vs-devin-desktop
- **Claude Code vs OpenAI Codex (2026)** — Claude Code (paid) — Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal and IDEs. Best for: Large, multi-step coding tasks from the terminal. OpenAI Codex (paid) — OpenAI's coding agent across ChatGPT, CLI, IDE extension and cloud; included in ChatGPT plans. Best for: Delegating tasks and automated PR review. Editorial comparison; rankings and picks are never sold. https://loadoutweekly.com/compare/claude-code-vs-openai-codex
- **Lovable vs Bolt.new (2026)** — Lovable (freemium) — Build full-stack web apps by chatting, with Supabase integration. Best for: Non-coders shipping a real web app. Bolt.new (freemium) — StackBlitz's in-browser prompt-to-app builder that runs code in WebContainers. Best for: Fast prototypes in the browser. Editorial comparison; rankings and picks are never sold. https://loadoutweekly.com/compare/lovable-vs-bolt-new

## New releases
- 2026-10-25 **farol** — Free, open-source (MIT) CLI and GitHub Action that runs after your AI code review and tells the human approver how risky a PR is: a 0-100 risk score, what the change reaches, untested lines and contract breaks, riskiest files first. Static analysis, never runs or uploads your code. TypeScript/React, Go, Python. Show HN Oct 25. Source: https://github.com/winnin/farol
- 2026-10-24 **AgentValley** — Free, open-source (MIT) Mac app that puts every Claude Code session and sub-agent in your MacBook's notch, each with its own pixel programmer, so you see who's working, on which model, and who's waiting on you. macOS 15+, Claude Code only. #4 on Product Hunt Oct 24. Source: https://www.producthunt.com/products/agentvalley
- 2026-10-23 **Corgi** — Terminal multiplexer built for coding agents: run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi in tabs that show which agent is working, needs you or is done, plus token tracking, file-change replay and worktrees. Free and open source (MIT); macOS, Linux and WSL. Show HN on Oct 23. Source: https://github.com/tals/corgi
- 2026-10-23 **Kimi K3.1 Pro** — Moonshot AI's new open-weight 3T-class model with a 1M-token context, post-trained for coding and agent work. Kimi reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (vendor numbers). A 2-3x faster Highspeed version ships too. Available now in Kimi.ai, Kimi Code and the Kimi API; full weights due by Nov 4. Source: https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro
- 2026-10-22 **Framer MCP** — Framer's official MCP server: connect Claude Code, Codex and other AI tools to Framer so your agent can work on the canvas, manage CMS content and publish your site, through a remote server with no local bridge needed. Source: https://www.framer.com/updates
- 2026-10-22 **1Password for Agents** — Lets supported AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT Work, Meta's Muse and others) sign in to your accounts without seeing passwords: you approve each login on your device and 1Password fills the password or one-time code. Included in 1Password Individual and Family plans, rolling out by agent. Source: https://1password.com/personal-ai-agent-integrations
- 2026-10-22 **Peras** — Set a usage line for your Claude Code or Codex plan and Peras warns, asks, or pauses the agent's tool calls once you cross it, so one long task can't burn your week. CLI and hooks are free and MIT; the native Mac menu bar app is a one-time 4.99 euros. On Product Hunt Oct 22. Source: https://www.producthunt.com/products/peras
- 2026-10-22 **Resend Inboxes** — API-first shared inboxes on your own domain for people and agents: threads, search, labels, drafts, webhooks and a configurable built-in agent, with Claude Code, Cursor and Codex connecting through MCP or skills. Free for up to 3 inboxes, then $1 per inbox on paid plans. On Product Hunt Oct 22. Source: https://resend.com/blog/announcing-inboxes
- 2026-10-22 **heal.dev** — Bug-hunting agent that learns how to run your app, builds a production-like sandbox with outside services mocked, and hunts for bugs, runtime vulnerabilities and performance issues. It only files what a failing test reproduces, and your coding agent can pull findings over MCP. Free during the beta, per the makers. #4 on Product Hunt Oct 22. Source: https://www.producthunt.com/products/heal-dev
- 2026-10-21 **Omnara** — Open-source managed agent platform, pitched as a self-hostable alternative to Claude Managed Agents: one API to deploy agents on any model and any machine. Apache 2.0 and free to self-host; Omnara Cloud has no platform fee, with models at provider token rates and machines billed by active time. Show HN on Oct 21. Source: https://www.omnara.com/pricing
- 2026-10-21 **Claude Security continuous scanning** — Claude Security now re-scans connected repos as code changes, marks findings fixed when the fix ships (and reopens them if they return), and adds an API and MCP. Public beta for Claude Enterprise only, with $25,000 a month in free usage credits for two months, through Dec 31, 2026. Source: https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-security-now-scans-continuously-and-tracks-fixes
- 2026-10-21 **Recursive Flint** — Open-weights coding model built to run on your laptop: 40B total / 2.5B active MoE, up to 512k-token context. Recursive reports 125+ tokens/s on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and top agentic coding scores for its size (vendor numbers). Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face; works with llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and SGLang. Source: https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint
- 2026-10-19 **Mercury 3** — Inception's diffusion LLM, 40x+ larger than Mercury 1, at 1,000+ tokens/s with a 1M-token context. OpenAI API compatible and on OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel. $0.20/M input and $0.70/M output (50% off at launch), with 100M free tokens on a new API key. Source: https://www.inceptionlabs.ai/blog/introducing-mercury-3
- 2026-10-18 **Sphinx** — Free, open-source Git hook that quizzes you on what your coding agent's diff actually does before a push goes through. Works with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode and Pi, using your agent, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible model. Show HN on Oct 18. Source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50137950
- 2026-10-17 **Ultracite v8** — Zero-config linter and formatter preset (Oxlint, Biome or ESLint) built to keep agent-written JS/TS consistent. v8 writes its rules once to AGENTS.md for every coding agent, and ultracite fix --claude or --codex hands leftover issues to that agent. Free and open source (MIT). On Product Hunt Oct 17. Source: https://github.com/haydenbleasel/ultracite/releases/tag/ultracite%408.0.1
- 2026-10-17 **NitroStack** — Full-stack platform for MCP servers: open-source TypeScript and Python SDK and CLI, NitroStudio to test tools visually, and NitroCloud hosting with GitHub deploys and scale-to-zero. Free Hobby plan (30k requests/mo); Pro $30/org/mo. #1 on Product Hunt's Oct 17 daily leaderboard. Source: https://nitrostack.ai/cloud/pricing
- 2026-10-16 **Cursor canvases and Environments API** — Cursor cloud agents can now build interactive canvases you share by link, a new Environments API (beta) creates and manages agent environments in code, and environments now hold up to 300 repos and load large setups 5x faster. Source: https://cursor.com/changelog
- 2026-10-16 **GBrain Tools** — From Garry Tan's YC-backed GBrain: connect Gmail, GitHub, Stripe and more once and use them in Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and your terminal without any AI seeing a password. Tools $19/mo per license; team workspace $199/mo. Source: https://gbrain.io/pricing
- 2026-10-16 **Parallax by Conifer** — Mac app (Linux daemon too) that runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents in one place: a Captain splits your ask across agents, built-in code review, and auto-fallback when one subscription hits its limit. Free to start with $50 of Conifer credit on GitHub sign-up. Source: https://www.conifer.build/parallax/
- 2026-10-16 **Pomerado** — YC-backed, open-source tool that turns any website (Google Flights, Zillow, legacy portals) into a tested API or MCP server for your agents, handling sign-in and 2FA. Free plan (100 tool calls/day); Premium $50/mo. Source: https://pomerado.ai
- 2026-10-16 **Harness by Autonomous** — Open-source command center for coding agents: run Claude Code, Codex and others across all your machines side by side, from a desktop app, terminal or phone (with voice). Free download; optional $149 desk device. #2 on Product Hunt's Oct 16 daily leaderboard. Source: https://www.producthunt.com/leaderboard/daily/2026/10/16
- 2026-10-16 **AI Sandboxes by Buddy** — Real Linux VMs for running AI-generated code and the apps it becomes, controlled via CLI, SDK, YAML or MCP, with snapshots and public endpoints. Source: https://www.producthunt.com/products/buddy/launches/ai-sandboxes-by-buddy
- 2026-10-16 **Polylane** — Production issue agent: maps your clouds, code and telemetry, catches pull requests that would break production, finds root causes and writes fixes. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex. Free plan; paid from $80/mo. Source: https://polylane.com/pricing
- 2026-10-16 **withHuman** — Open-source approval layer for AI agents: intercepts consequential tool calls and routes them through rules or a human reviewer. Hooks for coding agents and an MCP gateway. Open source free; cloud Scale plan $20/user/mo. Source: https://withhuman.ai
- 2026-10-16 **Navige** — Sits between your AI agents and the models/tools they pay for: caching, context trimming, loop guards and smart routing to cut agent costs. Free Watchtower plan; paid plans charge a share of savings. Source: https://www.producthunt.com/products/navige
- 2026-10-15 **Step 5 Preview (open weights)** — StepFun's flagship model for long-running agent and coding work: 600B total / 27B active MoE, up to 1M-token context, text and image input. Open weights on Hugging Face under the StepFun Model License 1.0, plus StepFun's API. Self-hosting needs data-center GPUs. Source: https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview
- 2026-10-15 **FLUX 3 Image Klein** — Black Forest Labs' 5.6B open-weights image model for text-to-image, editing and multi-reference generation (up to 10 images), with native 4K. Runs on GPUs with as little as 8GB VRAM (INT8); also in the BFL API. Source: https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3-image-klein
- 2026-10-15 **Nemotron 3.5 Super VL** — NVIDIA's open multimodal model for agents: 120B total / 12B active MoE, up to 1M-token context, text, image, document and video input, with tool use and coding.
